It loads the order through the OrderRepository abstraction, checks whether cancellation is allowed by calling the domain predicate canCancelOrder, tells the Catalog aggregate to release stock for each line item, and saves the order through the repository. The business rule itself lives in the domain function, so the use case only applies it. The file has no persistence code (no SQL or storage client), no transport or framework code, and no presentation logic. Note that execute never sets the order's state to cancelled. That looks like a functional bug, but it is not a responsibility placed in the wrong layer.
